questions.question: On the Day of Judgment, according to Surah Al-Waqiah, humanity will be divided into three distinct groups.
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states 'wa kuntum azwajan thalatha' — you will be in three groups. The surah identifies them as the Foremost (al-Sabiqun), the Companions of the Right Hand (Ashab al-Maimanah), and the Companions of the Left Hand (Ashab al-Mash'ama).

questions.question: What title does Surah Al-Waqiah give to the Foremost (al-Sabiqun) in verse 11?
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 declare 'wa al-sabiqun al-sabiqun, ula'ika al-muqarrabun' — the Foremost are precisely those brought nearest to Allah. Ibn Kathir identifies this as the highest of the three ranks described in the surah.

questions.question: The rhetorical question 'What are the Companions of the Right Hand?' in verse 8 is directed at which group?
options: The disbelievers on the Left Hand
The Companions of the Right Hand (Ashab al-Maimanah)
questions.explanation: Verse 8 asks 'wa ma ashab al-maimanah?' — the question is about the Companions of the Right Hand. The rhetorical form conveys the greatness and honor of this group, a device recognized across classical tafsir to signal a subject of supreme importance.

questions.question: According to verses 13-14, the Foremost rank in Paradise will include a large company from the earlier generations but only a few from the later generations.
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states 'thullatun min al-awwalin' (a large group from the former peoples) and verse 14 says 'wa qalilun min al-akhirin' (a few from the later peoples). Ibn Kathir records that the Companions were saddened when they heard this distinction about the Foremost rank.

questions.question: What three forms of torment are described for the Companions of the Left Hand in verses 41-43?
options: Scorching wind, boiling water, and shadow of black smoke
questions.explanation: Verses 41-43 describe the punishment as 'fi samum wa hamim' (scorching wind and scalding water) 'wa zill min yahmum' (and a shadow of black smoke). These three elements make up the torment prepared for the Companions of the Left.

questions.question: In verse 57, Allah uses the act of creating human beings as a logical argument for the possibility of resurrection after death.
questions.explanation: Verse 57 states 'Nahnu khalaqnakum falawla tusaddiqun' — We created you, so why do you not believe? The tafsir explains that initial creation from nothing is offered as the clearest proof that restoring life after death is well within Allah's power.

questions.question: At the moment of death, when the soul reaches the throat, who does Allah say is nearer to the dying person than those watching by the bedside?
questions.explanation: Verse 85 states 'wa nahnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum' — We (Allah) are nearer to him than you. This refers to the moment 'idha balaghat al-hulqum' (when the soul reaches the throat), emphasizing Allah's complete awareness and closeness at the time of death.

questions.question: Classical scholars describe the rhetorical question 'ma ashab al-maimanah?' in verse 8 as an example of which literary device used to convey the greatness of a subject?
questions.explanation: The form 'ma X?' in Arabic is a device of ta'zim — it magnifies the subject by implying its description is beyond ordinary words. Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir both recognize this rhetorical pattern across the Quran as a signal of supreme importance for what follows.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir records a hadith stating that the Companions of the Prophet were saddened when verse 14 revealed that only a few from the later generations would attain the rank of the Foremost.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith narrated via Tirmidhi in which the Companions felt grief upon hearing 'qalilun min al-akhirin' (a few from the later peoples) regarding the Foremost rank. The Prophet then reassured them about the honor of this smaller number.

questions.question: Verse 19 states that the drinks of Paradise will cause 'la yusadda'una anha wa la yunzifun.' What do classical scholars say these two phrases mean?
options: No boredom and no end to the drink
questions.explanation: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain 'la yusadda'una' as 'they will not get a headache from it' and 'la yunzifun' as 'they will not become intoxicated or lose their reason.' Unlike worldly wine, the drink of Paradise brings pleasure with no harmful effect.

questions.question: According to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah as reported by al-Tabari, the phrase 'al-hinth al-azim' (the great sin) in verse 46 refers specifically to shirk (associating partners with Allah).
questions.explanation: Al-Tabari reports that Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah all interpreted 'al-hinth al-azim' as shirk — the gravest of all sins. The verse describes the people of the Left Hand as those who persisted in this great sin throughout their lives.

questions.question: Verses 63-65 present the agricultural sign: humans plant seeds, but what does the Quran say would happen if Allah so willed, and what does this prove?
options: The crops would grow twice as large, proving Allah's generosity
The crops would turn to debris (hutam), proving that actual growth belongs to Allah alone
The rain would stop, proving Allah controls weather
The harvest would be stolen, proving this world is a test
questions.explanation: Verse 65 states 'law nasha'u la-ja'alnahu hutaman' — if We willed, We could make it debris. Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that while humans sow, Allah alone causes germination and growth, and this divine power over crops supports the argument for resurrection.

questions.question: The phrase 'jaza'an bima kanu ya'malun' in verse 24 uses the Arabic verb form 'kanu ya'malun.' What significance do contemporary scholars find in this verb form?
options: It indicates deeds done in secret
It refers only to the deeds of prophets and martyrs
It is the past-continuous form, indicating habitually and consistently performed righteous deeds
It implies deeds recorded by the left-hand angels only
questions.explanation: Wahbah al-Zuhayli notes that 'kanu ya'malun' is the past-continuous construction in Arabic, meaning 'they used to habitually do.' The reward of the Foremost is thus tied not to a single act but to a sustained lifetime pattern of righteous conduct.

questions.question: Contemporary scholars explain that the fire sign in verse 73 serves a dual purpose: as a reminder (tadhkira) of the Fire of Hell and as a practical provision (mata') for travelers and those who need it.
questions.explanation: Verse 73 states fire was made 'tadhkiratan wa mata'an lil-muqwin' — a reminder and a provision for travelers. Wahbah al-Zuhayli explains that earthly fire simultaneously reminds believers of the Hellfire and serves as a real worldly benefit, reflecting the Quran's integration of the spiritual and the practical.

questions.question: In describing the environment of the Companions of the Right Hand, which triad of blessings does Wahbah al-Zuhayli highlight in his commentary on verses 28-32?
options: Gold thrones, immortal youths, and rivers of honey
Silk garments, cool breezes, and fruit orchards
Extended shade, flowing water, and abundant fruit
Lofty mansions, flowing wine, and pure spouses
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir draws attention to 'zill mamdud' (extended shade), 'maa maskub' (flowing water), and 'kathirat al-fakiha' (abundant fruit) in verses 30-32 as the foundational comforts of Paradise — addressing shelter, thirst, and nourishment together.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb reads the phrase 'khafidah rafi'ah' in verse 3 as describing both a physical cosmic upheaval and a simultaneous moral reversal of fortunes on the Day of Judgment.
questions.explanation: In Fi Zilal al-Quran, Sayyid Qutb interprets 'khafidah rafi'ah' (lowering and raising) as operating on two levels: the physical collapse of the world's order and the moral inversion whereby the powerful are humbled and the humble are exalted, both occurring in a single divine moment.

questions.question: When a Companion of the Right Hand dies, what greeting does verse 91 indicate awaits them?
options: 'Udkhul al-janna bi-rahmatillah' (Enter Paradise by Allah's mercy)
'Salamun laka min ashab al-yamin' (Peace be upon you from the Companions of the Right)
'Anta min al-muqarrabin' (You are among those brought near)
questions.explanation: Verse 91 states 'fa-salamun laka min ashab al-yamin' — peace be upon you from the Companions of the Right Hand. Ibn Uthaymeen explains that this is a word of honor and reassurance given to the dying believer of this rank, contrasting sharply with the fate of the deniers described in the verses that follow.

questions.question: The surah closes in verse 96 with 'fa-sabbih bi-smi rabbik al-azim.' Which earlier verse does this closing command directly mirror, creating a structural symmetry in the surah?
questions.explanation: Verse 74 contains the identical command 'fa-sabbih bi-smi rabbik al-azim' after the cosmic signs section. Sayyid Qutb and Wahbah al-Zuhayli both note this deliberate repetition as a structural bracket — the call to glorify Allah frames the cosmic proofs and the surah's entire closing, reinforcing its thematic unity.
